\caption{{\small Weighted Permutation Test of Quasi-Independence}} {\small
	\begin{algorithmic}[1]
		\Statex {\bf Input:} $\mathcal{D}$ - sample, ${w}(x,y)$ - bias function, $T : \mathbb{R}^{2n} \to \mathbb{R}$ - a test statistic
		\Statex {\bf Parameters:} $B$ - number of permutations
		\State Generate $B$ permutations $\pi_1,..,\pi_{B} \sim P_{\mathcal{W}}$. 
		\State Compute the test statistic $T_0 \equiv T(\mathcal{D})$.
		
		\For{$i=1$ to $B$}		
			\State Compute the test-statistic for the permuted dataset, $T_i = T(\pi_i(\mathcal{D}))$.
		\EndFor
		\State {\bf Output:} $P_{value} \equiv \frac{1}{B+1} \sum_{i=0}^{B} \indicator{T_i \geq T_0}$.
		\end{algorithmic}
\label{alg:weighted_permutations}}

Define the neighbours of $\pi_t$ to be all permutations obtained from $\pi_t$ by a single swap, that is,

\[

\caption{{\small SIS Permutation Test of Quasi-Independence }} {\small
	\begin{algorithmic}[1]
		\Statex {\bf Input:} $\mathcal{D}$ - sample, ${w}(x,y)$ - bias function.
		\Statex {\bf Parameters:} $B$ - number of permutations.
		\State Compute $\mathcal{W}(i,j) = {w}(x_i,y_j), \quad \forall i,j=1,..,n$.
		\State Set $\pi_0$ the identity permutation $\pi_0(i) = i$.
		\For{$b=1$ to $B$}
		\State Initialize the importance sampling and weighted (unnormalized) probabilities \hspace{1cm} $\quad \quad P_{IS}(\pi_b)=P_{\mathcal{W}}(\pi_b)=1$.				
		\State Compute $V_i = Var\Big(\log(\mathcal{W}(i,1)),..,\log(\mathcal{W}(i,n))\Big), \quad \forall i=1,..,n$.
		\State Order the variables by decreasing order of $V_i$:  $V_{\sigma(1)} \geq ... \geq V_{\sigma(n)}$. 		
		\For {$i=1$ to $n$}
		\State Sample $\pi_{b}(\sigma(i))$ with probabilities: \\ \hspace{3cm} $Pr(\pi_{b}(\sigma(i))=j) \propto \mathcal{W}(\sigma(i),j) \prod_{k=1}^{i-1} \indicator{\pi_b(\sigma(k)) \neq j}$.
		\State Update the probability $P_{IS}(\pi_{b}) = P_{IS}(\pi_{b}) \times \frac{\mathcal{W}(\sigma(i),\pi_{b}(i))}{\sum_{j=1}^n  \mathcal{W}(\sigma(i),j) \prod_{k=1}^{i-1} \indicator{\pi_b(\sigma(k)) \neq j}}$ .
		\State Update the (unnormalized) probability $P_{\mathcal{W}}(\pi_{b}) = P_{\mathcal{W}}(\pi_{b}) \times  \mathcal{W}(\sigma(i),\pi_{b}(i))$ .		
		\EndFor		
		\EndFor		
		\State {\bf Output:} $P_{value}$ computed from the $P_{IS}(\pi_b),P_{\mathcal{W}}(\pi_b)$'s according to Equation \eqref{eq:IS_pval}.
	\end{algorithmic}
	\label{alg:sis_permutations}}
